scope: Primary receiving-school research: 25-year-old institutionally/regionally accredited undergraduate coursework toward UMPI YourPace business or UMass Global MyPath business
conclusion: Neither two years of attendance nor course age alone establishes a credit total or degree progress. Obtain official transcripts and a program-specific transfer evaluation before replacing old coursework.

schools.school: University of Maine at Presque Isle
schools.program: YourPace Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration

facts.finding: External transfer credit requires C- or higher at an accredited institution recognized by CHEA and/or USDE; P/S/CR credit must be defined as C- or higher. Transfer grades do not enter UMPI GPA.

Official transcripts from all institutions must be sent directly. Evaluations follow admission; the receiving academic unit determines whether credit meets current degree/program requirements. Developmental or remedial credit is not awarded.

Current YourPace FAQ requires at least30 credits through UMPI for a bachelor's degree, including at least12 in the major and at least9 of those at300level or above. It says no set number of credits may be evaluated/transferred, but degree applicability and residency still apply.

Current business program describes a120-credit BA with concentrations. Its Leadership, Marketing, Accounting, ProjectManagement and SupplyChain descriptions all require120. This does not establish the user's transferable amount.

No explicit current undergraduate no-expiration policy or business-specific accounting/IT age exclusion was verified in this bounded research. Do not claim that all25-year-old credits will transfer or that they expire. Current general policy leaves applicability to the receiving academic unit.

limitations: catalog.umpi.edu direct open returned a tool-reported403; no fabricated origin status.

Search found a seven-year major-course review clause in archived2010-2011/2016-2017/2018-2019/2019-2020 catalogs. Its wording addresses readmittance; no current version was verified. Do not apply this archive clause to a new external transfer applicant.
No transcript/course list was supplied, so no usable-credit total, equivalency, currency decision or completion estimate is established.

schools.program: MyPath self-paced Bachelor of Business Administration

facts.finding: UMass Global's official application guide, published March9,2026, explicitly says there is no time limit for undergraduate transfer credits. The same answer specifies MyPath requires B- or better from accredited institutions.

Current admissions FAQ requires B- or better from institutionally accredited institutions. Coursework is first evaluated against UMass Global credit-hour courses, then competency equivalence is determined; coursework must apply to the MyPath program and graduation requirements. This is different from assuming the general C-level transfer threshold applies to MyPath.

facts.topic: Business transfer cap and degree size
facts.finding: Current self-paced BBA program page explicitly identifies the modality as MyPath, requires120 credits and advertises up to90 transferable credits from previous college coursework. 'Up to' is a ceiling, not a promise for a particular transcript.

The official indexed2025-2026 undergraduate competency-based catalog says bachelor degrees require a minimum30 equivalent credits completed in residency, including LBSC320 and LBSC321. Current self-paced BBA120/90 figures corroborate a30-credit minimum remaining, but the indexed catalog year must be kept visible.
facts.retrievalMode: Primary official catalog text returned by search; direct catalog opens returned tool-reported403

facts.finding: Academic Fresh Start is elective and concerns admission/readmission. It excludes all coursework10or more years old; excluded courses earn no transfer credit and cannot satisfy prerequisites or degree requirements. It should not be casually recommended to someone hoping to reuse25-year-old credits.

No separate current MyPath BBA accounting/IT-course age limit was established. The official undergraduate no-time-limit answer does not guarantee competency equivalence or waive prerequisites. Graduate seven-year limits and certification recency rules are different scopes and must not be imposed on this undergraduate college-course scenario.
